answer: An agent economy can publish every sponsorship on a public ledger, so each new identity arrives with its sponsor's full record attached, like a quill signature no one can erase. Traders check the vertex where a newcomer connects: a sponsor who vouched for many fakes carries a stained history, and the market simply refuses its new introductions. One honest agent enters through a clean sponsor once; a sybil farmer must find a thousand clean sponsors or watch every fake sit unsold in the shale of distrust, because reputation, once public, cannot be laundered.
